title: HelperSSHCompletionParams
description: The completion probe for one line at one caret. cwd and line are the USER's, and they are the reason this command is composed from a fixed script rather than trusted: both arrive as quoted ARGUMENTS to it, which is a data question, and neither can become shell syntax. The line's maximum length is bounded by the composer (a command that outgrows its bound is refused as exec_too_long rather than sent to die in a remote execve), not here — a schema bound on a line would be a second, smaller authority for the same fact.

cwd.description: The session's current directory, from OSC 7. An argument to the script and never syntax.

line.description: The command line being completed, verbatim and unfinished. An argument to the script and never syntax.

pos.description: The caret's byte offset in the line.

limit.description: The caller's bound on candidates, applied by the script. Required: a default chosen here would be a second answer to a bound the caller already owns.

nonce.description: The invocation's frame marker: the script prints it around its answer and the caller accepts nothing else. It also rides the heredoc delimiter, so the delimiter cannot collide with the script's own text.
